Team —

Ahead of next week's QBR I pulled together a short market snapshot (attached) that summarizes the most relevant competitor moves in the last 6 weeks. High level:

- Fast-follow pricing adjustments from two smaller LLM API players (see tab "Pricing timeline"). Expect more aggressive per-token promotions in EMEA/US SMB segments.
- Major public model release last week (vendor: HeliosAI): a 70B model with a strong bench for short-context generation and lower latency claims. Early perf benchmarks look favorable on small prompt suites.
- AWS Marketplace refreshed onboarding flow for inference partners — reduced procurement friction for marketplace customers (PartnerOps note attached).

Implications for QBR / leadership talking points:
- We should call out that pricing promos are noise vs. durable cost advantage: highlight our dedicated/reserved economics and predictable SLOs.
- Note the new Helios model as a potential threat for low-latency demo scenarios; ops team should validate our latency advantage on 1–2 representative prompt sets.
- Marketplace changes increase inbound for midmarket prospects; Marketing should prep a short playbook for Marketplace-led trials.

Asks (please reply inline with owners & ETA):
1) Rachel — consolidate a one-slide counter that summarizes how our Dedicated and Optimize features protect unit economics vs. promo pricing (ETA Wed EOD).
2) Laura — can you add 2–3 data points (conversion/revenue lift) from recent Marketplace-sourced trials? (ETA Thu noon).
3) Karthik — validate latency bench vs. Helios on 2 prompts and flag any infra needs (ETA Thu EOD).

I attached a short PDF and the raw pricing timeline spreadsheet. We'll synthesize anything you add into a single leadership slide for the QBR.

Thanks —
Vivek

Quick bench update — ran two micro-benchmarks against Helios public inference endpoint and our Dedicated pool baseline:

Environment & prompts tested:
- Prompt A: single-turn search-rewrite (median output ~32 tokens)
- Prompt B: 3-turn summarization (median output ~110 tokens; KV reuse scenario)

Results (median latency, 95th):
- Helios endpoint: Prompt A 82ms (95th 190ms), Prompt B 220ms (95th 520ms)
- Redwood Dedicated (current prod config): Prompt A 68ms (95th 160ms), Prompt B 185ms (95th 420ms)

Observations:
- We retain a consistent latency lead (~15–20% median) on these prompts. The tail latencies are comparable.
- Helios performs competitively on single-turn short outputs; benefit grows for optimized kernels they expose for <64 token runs.

Immediate asks/actions:
- Ops: confirm we can reproduce Prompt B numbers at scale for a 50 QPS synthetic workload (I can own load spec if infra needs a ticket).
- Sales Ops (Rachel): we can call out these numbers in the QBR slide as a measured demo advantage; propose language: "median latency advantage on representative demos: ~15%".

I'll upload raw bench logs to the Drive link and tag the infra ticket if we need capacity profiling.

Thanks —
Karthik
